# spectre — hyper-optimized Spectre / Tile(1,1) einstein tiler

A from-scratch implementation of the target architecture identified in the
performance review of `necocen/spectre` (see `REVIEW.md` from the previous
session). Rust core + wgpu renderer, with a C mirror of the hot path used for
validation and benchmarking in the build container.

```
rust/
  spectre-core/    zero-dependency generator (the product)
    src/lib.rs       exact integer lattice, implicit traversal, hysteresis
                     cache, exact TileId identities + pick()
    src/tables.rs    AUTO-GENERATED exact substitution tables (gen_tables.py)
    src/bin/bench.rs benchmark suite
    src/bin/svg.rs   SVG export of any viewport
    tests/           validation against the reference generator
  spectre-view/    interactive infinite tiler for the GPU (wgpu instancing)
  spectre-wasm/    wasm-bindgen bridge (zero-copy instance buffers, picking)
web/index.html     self-contained browser app (WebGL2): color modes, Truchet
                   strands, exact-identity tile painting, hysteresis caching
gen_tables.py      table generator + proof of equivalence with the reference
bench.c, tables.h  C mirror of the traversal (measured numbers below)
```

## How every review finding is addressed

| Review finding (necocen/spectre) | This implementation |
|---|---|
| Boxed hierarchy, 7–8 heap allocs per cluster, recursive destruction | **No hierarchy exists at all.** Implicit substitution traversal over static tables; a traversal frame is 40 bytes on a fixed stack; a viewport query performs **zero heap allocations** |
| Geometry re-derived recursively (skeleton anchors, per-leaf vertex walks) | All child transforms, anchors and AABBs are **precomputed exactly** for all 32 levels at table-generation time; placement is table lookup + integer add |
| Floating-point drift / exact `HexValue` with runtime `sqrt(3)` | Coordinates live on the rank-4 integer module spanned by unit vectors at 0°/30°/60°/90°; rotation and mirroring are **integer matrix permutations**; `sqrt(3)/2` is a compile-time constant used only at emission |
| Per-vertex trigonometry in the shader (rotation + 3 sine color terms per vertex) | **Zero transcendentals on the GPU.** 12-entry `(cos,sin)` const LUT, mirror = sign flip, color = per-instance RGBA8 unpack |
| Fat instances | **16-byte instances**: `f32 x, f32 y, u32 rot|mirror|kind, u32 rgba8` |
| Full regeneration whenever the float viewport changes | `CachedRegion` with **35 % hysteresis margin**: regenerate only when the live viewport escapes the cached region; measured 5 regens per 240 panned frames |
| Repeated GPU uploads, up to 3 per frame | One persistent capacity-doubling instance buffer, **one upload per regen**, zero CPU/upload work on cached frames |
| Runtime lyon tessellation + unused normal stream | Static 14-vertex / 12-triangle mesh (ear-clipped offline, embedded); no tessellation dependency, no normals |
| Allocating, branch-heavy iterator; intersection-object AABB test | Fixed-capacity stack sized `(MAX_LEVEL+2)*8`; AABB test is 4 comparisons on a rect transformed with the `|M|` trick |
| Hardcoded 4× MSAA | 1× default (throughput baseline); trivially configurable in `spectre-view` |
| `opt-level = "z"` for WASM perf tests | Workspace ships a `release-wasm-speed` profile (`opt-level = 3`, fat LTO) |
| Benchmarks: levels 3–6 only, no ns/tile, no pan traces, no memory | `bench` reports ns/emitted-tile, Mtiles/s, materialization GB/s, random viewport queries against a level-24 root, 240-frame pan traces with/without hysteresis, parallel regen |

## Correctness

The substitution tables are generated by `gen_tables.py`, which:

1. re-implements the official algorithm (via shrx/spectre, the Python port of
   the SMKGS supplementary generator) in **exact integer arithmetic** on the
   lattice module, and
2. asserts, transform-by-transform, that its leaf output equals the verbatim
   float reference algorithm for N = 1..3 with Delta, Gamma and Psi roots.

The C and Rust traversals are then validated against that reference:
full-enumeration multiset match at N=3 (559 leaves), viewport-culling
cross-check against an independent brute-force filter, substitution-recurrence
tile counts for levels 0–6, and serial/parallel equivalence
(`cargo test` runs all of these).

Coordinates remain exact to level 32 — a patch of ~10²⁷ tiles — with i64
headroom (max translation component ≈ 5.6 × 10¹⁴).

## Measured performance (C mirror, single throttled container core)

```
enumerate level 8:      16,908,641 tiles      ~32 ns/tile (~31 Mtiles/s)
materialize level 8:    16.9 M instances      ~28 ns/tile, 0.57 GB/s written
viewport 200x200  @ level-24 root (~1.6e21 tiles):   0.16 ms/query
viewport 1000x1000                                    3.0 ms/query
viewport 5000x5000 (2.4 M tiles)                     70 ms/query
pan trace, regen every frame (16 k tiles/frame):     0.49 ms avg, 0.65 ms worst
pan trace, 35 % hysteresis:  5 regens / 240 frames,  0.025 ms/frame amortized
```

For context against the benchmark matrix from the earlier session: the
necocen Criterion suite measures spatial queries over a *materialized*
hierarchy at substitution levels 3–6; here a level-24 implicit root — fifteen
orders of magnitude more tiles — answers a 200×200 viewport query in 0.16 ms
with zero allocations. On your desktop expect roughly 3–5× these single-core
numbers, times a near-linear factor from `instances_in_parallel` (splits the
root's 8 subtrees across threads) for large regenerations. Run the same
matrix against Tatham's `spectre.c` (combinatorial-coordinate CPU baseline)
and `necocen/spectre` (wgpu baseline) on your machine for a like-for-like
comparison; the geometry hash in `tests/` is the cross-implementation
correctness anchor.

## The GPU story (RTX 3080)

Rendering is fully GPU-resident: one instanced indexed draw (36 indices ×
N instances), flat shading, no trig, 16 B/instance. A 3080 is fill-rate/
bandwidth bound here — at 64 MB per 4 M cached instances, buffer upload is
~2 ms over PCIe and happens only on hysteresis misses; steady-state panning
costs the CPU nothing and the GPU one draw call.

Because CPU generation runs at tens of millions of tiles/second and
regenerations are rare and incremental by design, moving *generation* to a
compute shader is deliberately deferred (as the review recommends: "optional
GPU compute only after the CPU implementation is measured"). If you later
want it: the traversal is a natural fit for a persistent-threads compute
kernel with a work-stealing frame queue in workgroup shared memory, writing
instances via an atomic append buffer, followed by `draw_indexed_indirect` —
the instance format and shader would not change.

## Build & run (your machine)

```bash
cd rust
cargo test  -p spectre-core --release      # validation suite
cargo run   -p spectre-core --release --bin bench
cargo run   -p spectre-core --release --bin svg -- 6 60 out.svg
cargo run   -p spectre-view --release -- 24   # interactive; arg = root level
```

Controls: drag = pan, wheel = zoom (clamped so the cached region stays under
4 M tiles), `E` = toggle edges, `Esc` = quit.

`spectre-view` pins `wgpu 0.20` / `winit 0.29`; if your local versions
differ, the API deltas are minor and confined to `main.rs`.

## Web app

The generator compiles to WASM and runs entirely client-side; there is no
server component. Build and serve:

```bash
cargo install wasm-pack                # once
wasm-pack build rust/spectre-wasm --target web --out-dir ../../web/pkg
cd web && python3 -m http.server       # open http://localhost:8000
```

What's in it, and why it's shaped this way as a base for further work:

* **Same 16-byte instance format end to end.** `query()` fills a buffer inside
  WASM linear memory and JS views it zero-copy before a single `bufferData`
  upload. One instanced WebGL2 draw renders fills; edges, Truchet strands and
  the paint overlay are additional instanced draws over the *same* instance
  buffer, so decoration costs no extra generation work.
* **Exact tile identity as the overlay keystone.** Clicking calls `pick(x,y)`,
  which returns the tile's exact integer-lattice pose `(kind, s, r, t0..t3)` —
  a drift-free, regeneration-stable hash key (components < 2^53 up to
  level 28, so plain JS numbers are lossless). The paint tool is a 30-line
  demonstration of the pattern any game state would use: a
  `Map(identity -> data)` overlay on top of the read-only infinite generator.
  Adjacency, territory rules, edge-matching legality all build on the same
  key without epsilon comparisons.
* **Truchet strands are per-shape, not per-tile.** Two families of radius-1/2
  arcs join midpoints of consecutive edges around alternating vertices,
  authored once in tile-local coordinates and instanced everywhere; the
  numeric check in the repo verifies every interior edge midpoint is shared
  by exactly two arc endpoints, i.e. strands continue seamlessly across tile
  boundaries, mirrored tiles included. Ribbon vertices carry radial normals
  so strand *width is a shader uniform* — restyling never rebuilds geometry.
* **Curved spectre outline (default on).** The tiling structure is the
  spectre tiling either way — the substitution places a single chirality, no
  reflected tiles — but the "Curved (Spectre) outline" toggle swaps the
  straight Tile(1,1) boundary for the curve that makes chirality geometric:
  each unit edge becomes an S-curve `h*sin(2*pi*t)` along the edge normal,
  symmetric under 180-degree rotation about the midpoint (neighbors interlock
  exactly) and mirror-asymmetric (a reflected tile cannot fit). Verified: the
  curved boundary is self-intersection-free, preserves the exact tile area
  3+3*sqrt(3) (the sine offsets cancel), passes through every straight-edge
  midpoint (Truchet anchors stay valid), and ear-clips to the full 110
  triangles. It is a mesh-only swap: instances, identities and picking are
  unchanged (picking uses the straight polygon, so clicks within ~0.125 of a
  curved boundary may resolve to the neighbor).
* **Color modes are shader-side** (substitution label, 24-orientation hue,
  mystic pairs, label hue, flat): switching never touches the CPU. A "mirror
  parity" mode would be a solid color by the chirality property above, so the
  slot highlights the Gamma1/Gamma2 mystic pairs instead.
* **Same hysteresis caching as the native renderer**, with the margin
  auto-shrunk so the cached region respects the configurable tile budget, and
  zoom-out clamped to that budget.

Extension seams left deliberately open: the `meta` word has 25 free bits for
per-tile game state; `for_each_ids_in` streams exact identities for
region-scale logic (flood fills, scoring); the paint overlay generalizes to
any `identity -> render override` layer; and `sendPrompt`-style UI hooks,
multiplayer sync of the overlay map, or an SVG/PNG plotter all sit on top of
the same two calls (`query`, `pick`).

Regenerating tables (only needed if you change `MAX_LEVEL` or the rules):

```bash
python3 gen_tables.py   # rewrites tables.h and rust/spectre-core/src/tables.rs
```
